name: Orecchiette with Italian sausage, chard, and melted leeks
intro: The classic way orecchiette is eaten in southern Italy — with sausage and bitter greens — made with November's leeks and chard. The sausage browns first, and its fat melts the leeks.
needs: ¾ lb Italian sausage, casings removed
1 bunch Swiss chard, stems chopped, leaves torn
Salt, black pepper, and chile flakes

steps.text: Bring a big pot of well-salted water to a boil.

Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into bite-sized pieces, until it's browned and cooked through. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and pour off all but about a tablespoon of the fat.
Lower the heat to medium-low, add the butter, leeks, and a pinch of salt, cover, and cook, stirring now and then, until the leeks are soft and sweet.
Uncover, add the chard stems, garlic, and a good pinch of chile flakes, and cook until the stems are tender.
Boil the orecchiette until just tender. Before you drain it, scoop out a cup of the pasta water.
Stir the chard leaves into the skillet until wilted. Add the pasta, the sausage, half the Parmesan, and a splash of pasta water, and toss over the heat until glossy.
The rest of the Parmesan, black pepper, and a squeeze of lemon.

how_it_works: Sausage seasons the whole dish: a spoonful of its fat cooks the leeks, and the bits stuck to the pan dissolve into the sauce. Leeks cooked low and covered don't brown; they melt. Starchy pasta water and Parmesan, tossed over the heat, pull it all together without cream. Chard stems go in before the leaves because they need longer.
swaps: A can of white beans instead of the sausage, for a meat-free night.
Ground turkey with a pinch of chile and garlic, if you'd rather skip pork.
Shredded leftover braised chicken instead of the sausage.
leftovers: Pack a bowl for lunch. It's best warmed in a skillet with a splash of water.
